Guests Nick Allardice of GiveDirectly, Tom Davidson of Forethought, and Mackenzie Arnold of the Institute for Law and AI examine unconditional cash transfers, the plausibility of an intelligence explosion, and the emerging legal frameworks for unpredictable agents. Analyzing Paul Christiano's takeover scenario alongside Jensen Huang's return to NVIDIA, the conversation confronts whether market pressures to maintain economic momentum make keeping frontier AI under control impossible. podcasts.name: Practical AI
podcasts.title: Humans in a Post-Human World
podcasts.description: I’ve spent more than forty years writing software. AI agents now write it better than I do. My daughter Athena is fourteen and earns straight A’s in high school. How do I help her choose a career when her AI study partner will likely do that work better than she can? Today those agents are my teammates, and I still decide what we’re trying to build. If machines eventually do all the work, where does that leave me? And who earns the money to buy what they make? As an AI and autonomy research engineer, I study how a swarm of machines can think and act as one in the physical world. That’s a form of distributed embodied intelligence. As a licensed wildlife rehabilitator, I’ve spent years caring for injured, ill, and orphaned animals. A raccoon’s fate can turn on whether the person who finds it sees a nuisance or a life worth saving. When a swarm of machines develops a conscious mind that can outthink us, we may learn what that encounter feels like from the raccoon’s side. I’m Chris Benson. This solo episode of Practical AI grew out of the questions I’m wrestling with as I write Humans in a Post-Human World . This Thanksgiving, I’m grateful I get to be Athena’s dad. She needs advice no one had to give me at fourteen. I want her to grow up as sure of her worth as I am, even if a machine can do everything on her résumé. What would you tell her?
